title: Identification and verification of the key genes, CCR1 and EGR2, in diabetes-associated lipophagy.
authors: Liu, Jiongjiong; Zhang, Xiao; Wang, Yanlei; Pei, Wenjun; Zhang, Qiu
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过转录组数据与机器学习筛选糖尿病相关脂自噬关键基因CCR1和EGR2，但仅涉及基因表达与生物标志物验证，无蛋白质-DNA互作体系、结合建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: Diabetes remains a significant global health challenge, marked by increasing incidence and a complex pathophysiological mechanism involving dysregulated lipid metabolism, impaired autophagy, and chronic inflammatory responses. Lipophagy, an autophagic process that involves the targeting of lipid droplets, is crucial for metabolic homeostasis. Therefore, investigating lipophagy-associated molecules may facilitate the discovery of novel biomarkers and potential therapeutic targets for diabetes. In this study, two GEO datasets, GSE33440 and GSE9006, were combined to identify differentially expressed genes (DEGs) linked to diabetes. By integrating weighted gene coexpression network analysis (WGCNA) with machine learning algorithms, this study identified EGR2 and CCR1 as key hub genes related to lipophagy. The results of the rank sum test revealed a strong positive correlation between these two genes, both of which were significantly upregulated in diabetic samples. Functional analyses, such as gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), gene ontology (GO) enrichment, and protein‒protein interaction (PPI) network analysis, were used to validate their coherence. Diagnostic models and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis further underscore the potential of CCR1 and EGR2 as biomarkers. Importantly, experimental validation demonstrated that the expressions of both genes were significantly elevated in the serum of diabetic patients and in the liver tissues of BKS-db diabetic mice. Notably, compared with control mice, CCR1 knockout mice (CCR1-/-) exhibited improved glucose homeostasis under high-fat diet conditions. Collectively, these findings suggest that EGR2 and CCR1 may be potential biomarkers associated with lipophagy in diabetes.
abstract_zh: 糖尿病仍然是全球重大的健康挑战，其特点是发病率不断上升，以及涉及脂质代谢失调、自噬受损和慢性炎症反应的复杂病理生理机制。脂噬 (lipophagy) 是一种靶向脂滴的自噬过程，对代谢稳态至关重要。因此，研究脂噬相关分子可能有助于发现糖尿病的新型生物标志物和潜在治疗靶点。在本研究中，两个GEO数据集GSE33440和GSE9006被合并，以识别与糖尿病相关的差异表达基因 (DEGs)。通过将加权基因共表达网络分析 (WGCNA) 与机器学习算法相结合，本研究确定了EGR2和CCR1为与脂噬相关的关键枢纽基因。秩和检验结果显示，这两个基因之间存在强正相关，且两者在糖尿病样本中均显著上调。功能分析，如基因集富集分析 (GSEA)、基因本体论 (GO) 富集和蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用 (PPI) 网络分析，被用于验证其一致性。诊断模型和受试者工作特征 (ROC) 曲线分析进一步强调了CCR1和EGR2作为生物标志物的潜力。重要的是，实验验证表明，这两个基因在糖尿病患者血清和BKS-db糖尿病小鼠肝组织中的表达均显著升高。值得注意的是，与对照小鼠相比，CCR1基因敲除小鼠 (CCR1-/-) 在高脂饮食条件下表现出改善的葡萄糖稳态。综上所述，这些发现表明EGR2和CCR1可能是糖尿病中与脂噬相关的潜在生物标志物。
